summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a 2D top-down pixel-art simulation game developed in Godot Engine 4 that puts players in charge of building and sustaining a human outpost on the Moon and Mars. Designed as an accessible mission simulator for aspiring explorers, the game challenges players to balance four interconnected survival systems: life support (oxygen and water), power generation, radiation shielding, and closed-loop food production.

It addresses the challenge by turning complex off-world habitat engineering and environmental hazards into intuitive, real-time decision-making. Through a live telemetry HUD and retro 8-bit visuals, players immediately see how resource shortages or radiation spikes impact colony survival.

This project is important because it makes space exploration science approachable and engaging for students and the public, fostering systems-level thinking and inspiring the next generation of aerospace problem-solvers.
details:
Overview & How It Works Our project is a 2D top-down pixel-art simulation and resource-management game where players build, operate, and sustain a human outpost on the Moon and Mars. Players explore a tile-based colony map, construct and upgrade essential habitat modules, and actively balance four interlocking survival systems: life support (oxygen and water recycling), power generation and storage, radiation shielding, and closed-loop food production. Through a real-time HUD, players monitor vital colony metrics, allocate limited resources, and respond to environmental hazards before critical systems fail.

Benefits Closed-loop life support and off-world habitat engineering are complex, multidisciplinary challenges that can feel abstract to newcomers. Our game translates these systems into an intuitive, hands-on interactive experience, allowing players to immediately observe how an imbalance in one subsystem—such as a power drop or insufficient shielding—cascades across oxygen supply, crop yields, and crew survival.

Intended Impact By turning real space-exploration constraints into engaging gameplay, the project aims to spark STEM curiosity and systems-level thinking among students, educators, and space enthusiasts. It bridges technical concepts behind sustained lunar and Martian missions with accessible interactive storytelling, helping players appreciate the engineering trade-offs required for humanity to live and work beyond Earth.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Game Engine & Language: Godot Engine 4 and GDScript, structured around a modular, event-driven architecture (GameManager and SignalBus autoloads) for scalable state and resource tracking.
  • Design & Gameplay Systems: Custom 2D pixel-art sprites and tilemaps, an interactive HUD for live telemetry, scene transitions from a title menu and intro cutscene into core outpost gameplay, and 8-bit chiptune background audio.
  • Scientific Reference & Environment: Mission concepts and environmental constraints informed by NASA lunar and Martian surface data (solar radiation, day-night power cycles, and in-situ resource needs).

Creativity Instead of presenting space-habitat management as a dense spreadsheet or static dashboard, we combined the approachable, cozy top-down aesthetic of classic pixel-art life-sim games with authentic aerospace survival mechanics. Pairing retro 8-bit visuals and music with real engineering dilemmas makes extreme-environment problem-solving both memorable and fun.

Key Factors Considered

  • Realism vs. Accessibility: Balancing authentic lunar and Martian hazards (radiation exposure, energy bottlenecks, and closed-loop resource limits) with clear visual feedback so players can grasp cause-and-effect without prior aerospace training.
  • Clarity of Feedback: Designing a clean, readable HUD and distinct visual cues on the base map so players can diagnose shortages and prioritize repairs under pressure.
  • Modular Architecture: Building decoupled scripts and signal-based communication in Godot 4 so new habitat modules, planetary scenarios, and hazard events can be expanded smoothly.
